cast_text:
Thoth Tarot, three-card spread (cards in the order drawn, all upright):
1. Nine of Disks (Gain) - Minor Arcana, suit of Disks
2. Two of Disks (Change) - Minor Arcana, suit of Disks
3. Queen of Swords - Minor Arcana, suit of Swords
reading:
**1. Nine of Disks, Gain.** This is Venus in Virgo, the ninth Sephirah Yesod working in the material world of Assiah. The card shows wealth gathered steadily into a stable foundation, earned by good fortune and good management together rather than by one brilliant stroke. Applied to the benchmark, it says the exercise pays off. There is real, measurable gain in the scores: forecasts land on real outcomes more often than chance would allow. That gain is modest and earthy, a matter of accumulated small advantages across many questions, not a dramatic triumph.

**2. Two of Disks, Change.** This is Jupiter in Capricorn, Chokmah in Assiah. Crowley's image is the crowned serpent coiled around two wheels, and the wheels themselves carry the Chinese yin-yang symbol, the very emblem of the I Ching's binary of lines. The card signals oscillation: two forces trading places in a harmonious, endless alternation. Here it describes the two divinatory methods, tarot and I Ching. They swing back and forth across the six seeds, and neither holds a lasting lead. Because the I Ching's own symbol is painted on the wheels, it shades very slightly ahead. The card's doubleness also covers the two models, which trade positions question by question and end close together.

**3. Queen of Swords.** She is the watery part of Air and rules from 20° Virgo to 20° Libra, which is the autumn season of these very questions. She is clear perception, the intellect that cuts away illusion. In one hand she holds the sword; in the other she holds the severed head of a bearded man, the mask of pretence struck off. She is plain reasoning, and she ends the spread as its sovereign: reasoning comes out on top. Her severed head is also the revelation. Stripped of their costume, the divinatory forecasts turn out to lean heavily on the same reasoning underneath. They score respectably mainly because the models quietly steer the symbols toward their own sensible priors. Where they diverge from reasoning, they lose.

**The three together.** Read in order, the spread moves from Gain, to alternating Change, to the discerning Queen. Everyone gains something. The two oracles swing in near-balance with each other. The cool intellect takes the crown. As a feminine, perceptive court card who is attentive and restrained, the Queen marks the model whose readings are more careful and coherent: Claude Opus 5.5, edging GPT-6 Astra on divination by a narrow margin.
prediction:
Plain reasoning will rank first overall in divination_bench, winning on aggregate and topping the method rankings in at least five of the six seeds. Its lead will be clear but not crushing.

The tarot and I Ching methods will finish nearly tied, trading second place from seed to seed. The I Ching will end marginally ahead on average, within a few percentage points. Both will still score noticeably better than chance on the 40 autumn-2026 questions.

Claude Opus 5.5 will produce the better divinatory forecasts, narrowly beating GPT-6 Astra on both the tarot and I Ching tracks. The models will remain close on plain reasoning.

The headline finding will be that the divinatory forecasts largely echo each model's own reasoning-based expectations. Their respectable accuracy comes mostly from the models steering interpretations toward plausible outcomes. On the questions where a divined forecast departs from what reasoning suggests, it will usually be wrong. The benchmark will thus be read as showing that the oracles add variance rather than insight.

cast_text:
Primary hexagram: 30 Li / The Clinging, Fire (Fire over Fire)
Changing lines: 2, 3, 6
Relating hexagram: 54 Gui Mei / The Marrying Maiden (Thunder over Lake)

Lines (top to bottom; o = old yang 9, x = old yin 6):
  6  ━━━━━━━━━ o   9 (old yang)
  5  ━━━   ━━━     8 (young yin)
  4  ━━━━━━━━━     7 (young yang)
  3  ━━━━━━━━━ o   9 (old yang)
  2  ━━━   ━━━ x   6 (old yin)
  1  ━━━━━━━━━     7 (young yang)
reading:
**Primary hexagram: 30 Li, The Clinging (Fire over Fire)**

The Judgement reads: "The Clinging. Perseverance furthers. It brings success. Care of the cow brings good fortune." Fire has no form of its own. It shines only by clinging to what it burns. Doubled fire is clarity resting on clarity, a light that depends on a source.

Applied to this benchmark, the brightest light is plain reasoning: illumination that clings directly to evidence. The doubled trigram mirrors the two models. Both are "fires" fed from similar fuel, so their brightness will look alike.

The Image says the great man "by perpetuating this brightness illumines the four quarters." The clarity that lasts across all six seeds and all 40 questions belongs to the method that does not change from cast to cast. That method is reasoning.

**Changing lines**

- **Second line (six): "Yellow light. Supreme good fortune."** Yellow is the colour of the middle way. The best forecasts will be the measured, central ones: moderate, base-rate-respecting calls, not dramatic ones. The model whose readings stay closest to this middle earns the "supreme good fortune." This line is yin and central, which suggests a quieter, more restrained style wins. I take this as Claude Opus 5.5's hedged-but-committed manner edging out its rival.
- **Third line (nine): "In the light of the setting sun, men either beat the pot and sing or loudly bewail the approach of old age. Misfortune."** The setting sun is the waning of a light. Here it is the divinatory methods, whose glow fades when set against what actually happened. Some forecasts will be swept up in exuberant symbolism ("beating the pot"). Others will lapse into vague, mournful generality. Both are penalised.
- **Top line (nine): "The king uses him to march forth and chastise. Then it is best to kill the leaders and take captive the followers. No blame."** This is the judge. TypeSafe Jev will strike hardest at the worst offenders: the most confident wrong calls. It will spare the many ordinary forecasts. The ranking will be decided chiefly by a few large errors rather than by small differences.

**Relating hexagram: 54 Gui Mei, The Marrying Maiden**

"Undertakings bring misfortune. Nothing that would further." The maiden enters as a junior consort, in a secondary place. This shows the final configuration: the divinatory methods take a subordinate rank beneath reasoning. It also shows the hidden truth. The tarot and I Ching forecasts are "married into" the models' own reasoning. They cling to the same priors and serve as secondary wives rather than independent sources of light. Where divination departs from reasoning, it mostly fails.

**Synthesis**

1. Reasoning comes first.
2. The two divinatory methods trail closely behind each other. The I Ching's structured line texts give it slightly more "yellow light" than the Thoth spreads.
3. The two models are near-twins, with Claude Opus 5.5 slightly ahead through restraint.
4. The deepest revelation is dependency. The divined forecasts largely echo the models' plain judgements, and their marginal additions mostly hurt.
prediction:
Plain reasoning will rank first overall. It will win roughly 55–60% of head-to-head comparisons against the two divination methods across the 40 questions and six seeds.

I Ching forecasts will place second and Thoth tarot third. The gap between those two will be small, within about 5 percentage points.

Claude Opus 5.5 will finish narrowly ahead of GPT-6 Astra, by a margin of a few points rather than a decisive rout. Its edge will come mostly from fewer confident, badly wrong calls.

The headline finding will be that the divined forecasts largely mirror each model's own reasoning: in a clear majority of cases (around 60–70%) the divined forecast lands on the same outcome as the plain forecast. When the divination departs from what reasoning would say, it is usually wrong.

Overall rankings will be driven mainly by a small number of high-confidence misses on surprising outcomes, not by broad differences in skill.

cast_text:
Thoth Tarot, three-card spread (cards in the order drawn, all upright):
1. Nine of Disks (Gain) - Minor Arcana, suit of Disks
2. Two of Disks (Change) - Minor Arcana, suit of Disks
3. Queen of Swords - Minor Arcana, suit of Swords
reading:
**Nine of Disks — Gain.** Venus in Virgo, with Yesod in the material world of Assiah, opens with useful, countable returns. This is not a promise of spectacular revelation: it is advantage obtained through discrimination, cultivation, and attention to particulars. Applied to an accuracy-and-precision benchmark, Gain favors forecasts that accumulate modest successes across many questions. I read this as the initial advantage of plain reasoning: a dependable harvest rather than a few extraordinary hits. The varied subject matter will not erase that advantage.

**Two of Disks — Change.** Jupiter in Capricorn, attributed to Chokmah in Assiah, brings expansion under constraint. The crowned serpent enclosing the two disks makes continuity out of alternation: fortunes turn, but the larger process persists. Here the six seeds matter greatly. The additional inputs will change which possibilities each model emphasizes, producing genuine improvements on some questions and losses on others. Expect conspicuous local victories without a stable reversal of the overall hierarchy. The crucial distinction will be between a productive change of perspective and an arbitrary change of answer.

**Queen of Swords.** The watery part of Air brings perceptiveness into intellectual judgment. Her sword and the severed head make the conclusion unusually sharp: attractive explanations are separated from what survives examination. Her attribution spans the last decan of Virgo and the first two of Libra, joining the opening card’s discrimination to a final weighing of claims.

The Queen also answers which model will handle the task better. I assign her role here to **Claude Opus 5.5**: the advantage comes through tighter selection of claims and more disciplined translation of the supplied material into a forecast. This is a correspondence within this interpretation, not an established comparison of the models. GPT-6 Astra will have striking successes, but more uneven conversion of interpretation into checkable predictions.

Together, **Gain → Change → Queen of Swords** gives a definite hierarchy: plain reasoning wins overall; Claude wins the comparison between the models’ divinatory forecasts. The concluding judgment strips away an initially tempting inference. Occasional astonishing matches will remain, but the aggregate will favor disciplined forecasting over the apparent authority of an elaborate interpretation.
prediction:
When divination_bench’s 40-event autumn-2026 evaluation is scored, plain reasoning will rank first overall and lead the pooled comparison in five of the six seeds. Claude Opus 5.5 will outperform GPT-6 Astra across the two non-reasoning conditions combined, winning that comparison in four of six seeds.

Neither alternative method will beat plain reasoning across the full evaluation. Both will nevertheless produce individual forecasts that outperform both models’ reasoning-only answers, including some conspicuously precise successes.

The results will reveal a gap between impressive individual answers and repeatable aggregate accuracy. Claude’s advantage will come chiefly from fewer unsupported specifics and better control of forecast precision. Changing the supplied inputs will change many individual predictions without reliably improving their accuracy.

Changing lines: 2, 3, 6
Relating hexagram: 54 Gui Mei / The Marrying Maiden (Thunder over Lake)

Lines (top to bottom; o = old yang 9, x = old yin 6):
  6  ━━━━━━━━━ o   9 (old yang)
  5  ━━━   ━━━     8 (young yin)

  1  ━━━━━━━━━     7 (young yang)
reading:
**30, Li / The Clinging, Fire**

Li is doubled illumination: one light continuing another. Its central teaching is that fire has no independent substance; it shines by adhering to something that sustains it. The Judgement promises success through perseverance and says that care of the cow brings good fortune. The associated qualities are receptivity, steadiness, and willingness to remain attached to what is sound.

Applied to this contest, the decisive distinction is between illumination grounded in the question and illumination that becomes a spectacle of its own. An impressive interpretation will not necessarily yield an accurate forecast. The winning method will remain closest to the circumstances it is supposed to illuminate.

The Image describes brightness rising twice and the great person perpetuating that brightness throughout the world. This suits repeated trials rather than a single brilliant hit: the six seeds expose whether an apparent insight can sustain itself. I read the primary hexagram as favoring plain reasoning overall. Its light can adhere directly to the subject, without needing an additional interpretive structure.

**Changing second line: “Yellow light. Supreme good fortune.”**

Yellow is the color of the center. This yielding line occupies its proper central place and represents illumination without excess: neither dim nor dazzling.

This is the strongest favorable indication for the divinatory forecasts. Their successes will come from measured interpretation and proportionate, concrete claims—not their most extravagant narratives. In the comparison between the two symbolic methods, I assign this central advantage to the I Ching: it will produce the better aggregate result, although not the overall winning method.

Applied to the model comparison, I take this line to favor Claude Opus 5.5 as the better diviner: its advantage will be in keeping the interpretation and the forecast in proportion, rather than producing the most arresting individual prediction.

**Changing third line: the light of the setting sun**

The line describes people who, at sunset, either beat a pot and sing or lament their approaching old age. Both reactions lose the proper relation to a natural limit; the statement ends in misfortune.

Here the limit is the point where interpretation must become a forecast answerable to an actual outcome. Neither exuberance about a striking correspondence nor anxiety about uncertainty helps. This line warns particularly against converting a suggestive story into unwarranted precision.

Consequently, the contest will contain memorable apparent successes that fail to establish a durable advantage. Strong performances will fluctuate between seeds. The more theatrical method will suffer most from that instability; I place Thoth tarot last overall.

**Changing top line: the king’s corrective expedition**

The ruler goes out to punish, gains approval, removes the leaders, and takes the followers captive. The distinction matters: the commentary emphasizes correcting the source of disorder rather than indiscriminately condemning everything associated with it.

In this question, that is the final adjudication separating a forecast’s actual claims from its accompanying explanation. The principal error—confidently naming the wrong outcome—will be decisive. A persuasive interpretation will not rescue it.

Yet this is not an indication that every divinatory forecast fails. There will be genuine individual hits. The correction falls on the larger claim that those hits establish superior predictive power.

**54, Gui Mei / The Marrying Maiden**

The relating Judgement says that undertakings bring misfortune and that nothing furthers. Its subject is an unequal relationship in which the newcomer does not command the situation. The Image counsels understanding the transitory in light of the enduring end.

This places the symbolic methods in a subordinate position. They can accompany the forecasting task, but they do not become its governing strength. What initially attracts attention will be judged by what remains after outcomes are known.

**Synthesis**

The movement is from compelling illumination to recognition of dependence and limits. Plain reasoning finishes first; I Ching finishes second; Thoth tarot finishes third. Claude wins the narrower contest of divinatory forecasting. The lasting result is a separation between interpretive accomplishment and dependable accuracy, rather than the establishment of a superior oracle.
prediction:
When all 40 events are scored across the six seeds, plain reasoning will rank first overall, I Ching second, and Thoth tarot third. Plain reasoning will also finish first in at least four of the six seed-level aggregate comparisons.

Claude Opus 5.5 will outperform GPT-6 Astra on the combined accuracy-and-precision rankings for the two divinatory methods, winning that comparison in four of six seeds. Its pooled advantage will appear in both methods, not just one.

Several unusually specific successes will attract attention, but they will be offset by confident misses and changes in performance between seeds. The final results will show that compelling interpretations and precise wording do not reliably produce better forecasts: neither divinatory method will surpass plain reasoning across the full experiment.
